hypotheses.priority: high; directly supported only on39f parent
hypotheses.statement: Small systematic errors in learned relaxation z accumulate over shallow recovery tails; equilibrium u error contributes separately.
hypotheses.test: FrozenA0 andA6 per-gate/per-channel u-only,z-only,both and teacher-state-reset oracles; repeat with corrections restricted to rise, plateau or recovery and reset intervals1/8/64 ticks. Record signed crossing shifts, log_z bias and state error growth. Oracles diagnostic only.
hypotheses.falsifier: Current-candidate z correction does not preferentially recover timing or both/reset fail the reference floor; then z accumulation is insufficient or the contract needs investigation.

hypotheses.statement: LR0.001 and joint shared-feature updates damage already-good coefficients faster than they refine residual slow dynamics, causing step0 selection.
hypotheses.test: Factorial LR0.001 versus0.0001 and all-parameter versus z-output-head-only updates from identical A0 weights with reset Adam; record coefficient drift, clipping and per-term gradient cosines. Check early steps100/300/1000 in addition to normal checkpoints.
hypotheses.falsifier: LowerLR and z-only updates do not improve optimization/passing cases or preservation despite measured smaller coefficient drift; this mechanism is not sufficient. z-only failure is conditional on the frozen feature basis.

hypotheses.statement: Mean normalized log_z loss can hide localized signed errors in slow, current-sensitive regimes even though every gate is supervised.
hypotheses.test: Keep original mean loss and add a fixed FIT-only worst-bin relaxation auxiliary: partition by gate and preregistered log_z bins, aggregate squared normalized rate errors within bins, use smooth maximum with fixed temperature. Compare auxiliary off/on with matched batches; equal total initial main/aux gradient calibration. Inspect all gates, not only failing development channels.
hypotheses.falsifier: Worst-bin FIT/independent rate-grid error decreases but current timing does not, or no improvement at matched optimization budget. In the former case rate approximation quality is not the sole bottleneck.

hypotheses.statement: Previous independent support expansion may not specifically cover the small-z, long-relaxation regimes that determine offsets.
hypotheses.test: Two paired sidecars replace a fixed fraction of training anchors/windows by independent FIT recovery-grid samples spanning all gates, log-spaced durations and initial displacement; compare to identical low-LR all-parameter arms with/without worst-bin objective. Same counts,updates and no copied development paths.
hypotheses.falsifier: Coverage audit confirms more occupied slow-regime bins and fitting improves, but held-out timing remains unchanged; missing support in those bins is insufficient. New cases remain training data, not independent confirmation.

hypotheses.priority: medium for conditioning; low for pureprecision

hypotheses.test: OnA0/A6 retain exact primary event rules and add signed onset/offset, slope, excursion identities, peak runner-up gaps, perturbation/phase probes and current/gate sensitivity. Route teacher coefficient probes separately for SK andNaTs; no rounding or relaxed eligibility.
hypotheses.falsifier: Timing events are well conditioned and per-gate corrections remove failure without ambiguity, or current errors follow a different identified source. Diagnostic phase changes never count as primary passes.
